cards.a: EVE-NG (Emulated Virtual Environment Next Generation) is a web-based lab platform that runs real images (IOS, NX-OS, ASA, and third-party VMs), with a free pro edition, ideal for big multi-vendor CCNP topologies.

cards.q: Why is EVE-NG well suited to large CCNP topologies?
cards.a: It is web-based, has a free tier, supports multiple real multi-vendor images on one platform, and offers browser console plus an API.

cards.q: Which image types can EVE-NG run?
cards.a: IOS/IOS-XE routers, NX-OS switches, ASA firewalls, vIOS-L2 for switching, Linux VMs as hosts, and containers for Linux nodes.

cards.q: What is the difference between EVE-NG Community and Pro editions?
cards.a: Community is a free basic tier, while Pro unlocks the image pool and image import; Pro+ is the licensed version.

cards.q: How do you run a lab in EVE-NG?
cards.a: Log in via the web UI, add a node, connect it, boot, open the console, and save the topology — all from the browser with no desktop app.

cards.q: Which collaboration and scaling features does EVE-NG offer?
cards.a: Multi-user support for team labs, an API for automation, snapshots to save states, templates for reuse, and external network connectivity to bridge to real networks.

cards.q: What hardware should you plan for an EVE-NG deployment?
cards.a: A Linux/ESXi host with many GB of RAM, disk for image storage, and CPU per node, scaled according to node count.

cards.q: How does EVE-NG compare to GNS3 and CML?
cards.a: EVE-NG uses a web UI, has a free tier, supports multi-vendor images, offers an API and high fidelity, and is best for large labs.

cards.q: What is the EVE-NG API endpoint used for automation?
cards.a: The EVE API is accessed via https://<host>/api/..., with snapshot and export handled through the UI.

cards.q: An EVE-NG node will not boot. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: The likely cause is an image problem, so check that the image is imported correctly for the node type.

cards.q: An EVE-NG console fails to open. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: The likely cause is a Java/HTML5 mode setting, so check the console mode being used.

cards.q: An EVE-NG API call returns a 401 error. What should you check?
cards.a: Check the authentication token, since an API 401 error is caused by an authentication problem.

cards.q: EVE-NG can only run Cisco images.
cards.a: False — EVE-NG supports multi-vendor images from Cisco and third-party vendors on one platform.

cards.q: What does the Pro edition of EVE-NG unlock that Community does not?
cards.a: The Pro edition unlocks the free image pool and the ability to import images such as Cisco QCOW files.

cards.q: Is EVE-NG a desktop application like GNS3?
cards.a: No — EVE-NG is entirely web-based; everything including console access is done from the browser.

cards.q: Which web-based free tool is best for large multi-vendor CCNP topologies with snapshots and API access?
cards.a: EVE-NG, which provides a free tier, real multi-vendor images, browser console, snapshots, and an API for big-scale labs.
